abstract: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture for every finite product of members of a two-parameter Dickson K3 family, with arbitrary allowed parameters, repetitions and CM specializations. The underlying Dickson construction and its real multiplication are due to van Geemen–Schütt. An explicit degree-sixty rational map from two independently varying conductor-fifteen curves, followed by a rotation and involution projections, gives a split algebraic comparison with two genus-four Jacobians. At jointly very general parameters the K3 has Picard number fourteen, transcendental rank eight and endomorphism field $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$; we determine its rational quadratic form and the rank-six diagonal specialization. The all-period extension uses the existing determinant correspondences of rStation paper 59. We prove ordinary HC for arbitrary finite products of abelian fourfolds with compatible $F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt5,\sqrt{-3})$ action and fixed signatures $(2,0),(1,1)$, for every Hermitian datum and period, together with two fixed CM elliptic curves. At a CM point the algebra generated by $F$ and the Hodge torus is split or quadratic over $F$. A joint common-norm calculation, adapted from paper 16, shows that its only relations with other factors are the supplied determinant relations. Connected norm kernels and an integral character check exclude hidden half-determinant classes. Tensor invariants then give the source-product theorem and transfer to the K3 products. Four exact CPU scripts accompany the proofs. Independent-pair generalized support, full Kuga–Satake algebraicity for the rank-eight RM K3, and the general Hodge conjecture remain open.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
change_summary: Strengthens Theorem B from individual all-powers and source-restricted mixed products to all finite products at arbitrary allowed parameters. New Theorem C proves ordinary HC for arbitrary products of F-fourfolds with the fixed pure/mixed signatures, all rational Hermitian data and all periods. Section 7 replaces the previous single-surface specialization case split by the CM algebra dichotomy, normalized embedded-field identification, the common-norm joint cocharacter argument adapted from paper 16, the connected-group and integral-character checks, and algebraic invariant generation from paper 59. Adds an exact 19-control CPU script and explicit prior-work comparisons. Retains all three reviewer clarifications: comparison with paper 28, Hodge versus Mumford–Tate group distinction, and generic-locus qualifications for the quadratic forms. No independent-pair generalized-support or full Kuga–Satake claim is added.

coauthors.contribution: Independent audit of the generic and diagonal rank/image arguments and rational forms; clarification of diagonal and definite-place reasoning; verification of ordinary-HC transfer and the source dichotomy; independent CM-field and joint-torus checks for the all-period extension, including the integral four-point central-intersection clarification; complete manuscript review.

title: A degree-sixty correspondence and Hodge classes on all finite products of a Dickson K3 family
